_about: Human spot-check of the local-model (ollama qwen3.5:9b) English for Rotterdam's street-name register, read against the Dutch. spotChecked lists every entry read; corrections replace the English of entries that were wrong or refused by the guard ({from} is the start of the Dutch it was written against); withheld drops a name with a reason. Repeated error classes were turned into repairs in scripts/lib/cityStreetNameOrigins.ts (gedempt, of/or, Naar, industriestad, ambacht, gegraven, verbastering, vlinderbloem) and the kept-Dutch-word guard rather than corrected one by one.

Graaf Florisstraat.en: Floris V, Count of Holland, 1254-1296, to whom the building of Schieland's Hoge Zeedijk near Rotterdam is largely owed.

Burgemeester s'Jacobplein.en: Frederik Bernard s'Jacob, 1850-1935, mayor (burgemeester) of Rotterdam 1893-1906.

Piekbrug.from: Deze brug is vernoemd naar de familie Piek
Piekbrug.en: This bridge is named after the Piek family, who owned property on Feijenoord at the end of the 18th century. A gentlemen's pavilion (herenkoepel) on Feijenoord is mentioned in 1769; it was later let, with the house beside it, to the Piek family. The pavilion was often used as a landing stage on rowing trips on the river, and members of the city government went there with their families to drink tea in summer. It came to be known as 'het koepeltje van Piek'. The Piekbrug crosses the Persoonshaven.

Dukdalfpad.from: In het water geplaatste zware paal
Dukdalfpad.en: A dukdalf (dolphin) is a heavy post in the water, braced by four to eight raking piles, for mooring ships or protecting bridges and locks.

Grote Hagen.from: Polder in het Land van Hagestein
Grote Hagen.en: Polder in the Land van Hagestein in the province of South Holland.

Ab de Molenaarpad.en: Ab de Molenaar (1921–1985), jazz musician, founder and leader of the jazz ensemble The Millers.

Goudenregenstraat.en: Laburnum (goudenregen), an ornamental shrub of the pea family.

Herastraat.en: Hera, Greek goddess and wife of the god Zeus.

De Krabbe.from: De Krabbe is een vlakte in de Maasmond
De Krabbe.en: De Krabbe is a shoal in the mouth of the Maas. It appears on Quack's chart of 1665 and on Tirion's map of 1748, among others, and was later called the Krabbeplaat.

Buizerdstraat.en: The buzzard (buizerd), a bird of prey.

Britsenburg.en: A corruption of Brittenburg, a former Roman fort near Katwijk aan Zee.

Ereprijsstraat.en: Speedwell (ereprijs), a small plant of the figwort family.

Antilopestraat.from: Herkauwer uit de orde der evenhoevigen
Antilopestraat.en: The antelope, a ruminant of the order of even-toed ungulates. This street was previously called Nicolaas Beetsstraat.

Beugstraat.from: Deze straatnaam is ontleend aan een schrobnet
Beugstraat.en: This street name comes from the beug, a trawl net used for anchovy fishing.

Boermarke.en: A boermarke is a piece of land owned in common by a number of farmers; a rural name given on the site of the former slaughterhouse.

Freerickshof.en: In 1882 Gerardus Adrianus Freericks (1825-1904) opened a pleasure garden, 'het Wapen van Holland', on the Dorpsstraat in Hillegersberg, popularly known as 'de tuin van Freericks'. From 1922 the building belonged to Louis van Zanten; it burned down on 23 January 1934. The streets lie on the site of the former pleasure garden.

Dokstraat.from: Deze naam herinnert aan de hier gelegen voormalige Dokhaven
Dokstraat.en: The name recalls the former Dokhaven here, dug in 1881 and filled in about a century later. The harbour was named after the municipal docks and ferries that lay here. Housing and the Dokhavenpark were built on the filled-in site.
